what.text: This page follows refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina living in Serbia and Kosovo, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 7697 refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina in Serbia and Kosovo, 31.2% of all refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Serbia and Kosovo is the largest host of refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by France and Denmark.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflicts in Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1992 to 1995, over Serb, Croat and Bihaca Krajina territory.
The conflict over Serb territory reached war level in every year from 1992 to 1995.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1992 at its highest figure, 349280 refugees.
It fell over the following decades; the main years of displacement in the data are 1992 to 1993 and 1996 to 2000.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Serbia and Kosovo.
These are year-end totals for Serbia and Kosovo only, reported to UNHCR.
